sources.entry: sh - A full-fledged subprocess replacement for Python.

summary.one_liner: sh is a Python subprocess replacement that lets you call any Unix program as if it were a function.
summary.what_it_does: The library lets Python code invoke external programs by name, as in `git("status", "--short")`, and returns their output. It is described as a full-fledged replacement for subprocess rather than a set of system commands reimplemented in Python. It depends on Unix system calls, so it runs on Linux, macOS, and BSDs. The README states that Windows is not supported. The README also links to full documentation and a single-page documentation version intended for LLM-assisted coding. Installation is a single pip install, and the developer section covers tox-based tests, building docs with Sphinx-style make commands, and coverage reporting.
use_cases: run shell commands from Python scripts
replace subprocess calls with a simpler syntax
automate git or other CLI tools from Python
wrap Unix command-line programs in Python functions
script system administration tasks on Linux or macOS
notable: Any installed program can be called as a Python function
Replaces subprocess with a more concise call syntax
Documentation available as a single page for LLM-assisted coding
Devcontainer and GitHub Codespaces setup for development
caveats: Does not support Windows; only Unix-like operating systems
Not a collection of system commands implemented in Python
